A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 43-page versions of the same research work. The main text, seven figures, equations, and Appendices A–E can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Appendix E reports original permutation-training experiments using networks with 50,000 hidden units and 1,000 test vectors. Figure 7 presents measured ensemble sizes and accuracies.

after.justification: Appendix E and Figure 7 retain these original permutation-training experiments and their measured results.

M1.justification: The template construction, orthonormal encoding, two-layer ReLU architecture, and iterative prediction, ensemble averaging, and rounding procedures are unchanged. The additional explanations and optimizer disclosure do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain permutation-training experiments in Appendix E and numerical execution checks for permutation, addition, and multiplication in Appendix B. No evaluated task, domain, or input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The numerical-versus-theoretical comparisons in Figures 5 and 7 are unchanged. No external competing method is newly evaluated; the added Malach citation appears only in related work.

E3.justification: Appendix E retains standard-basis training, 50,000 hidden units, 1,000 test vectors with two nonzero entries, and the same accuracy targets and input sizes. Full-batch gradient descent is newly disclosed, without revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The ensemble-size analyses in Figures 5 and 7 and numerical instruction-validation checks in Appendix B are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: There is no change to empirical seed or repeated-run information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing. Independent model averaging and the theoretical probability bounds already appear in v2.

E6.justification: Figures 5 and 7 retain identical result curves and findings, including empirical ensemble requirements below the theoretical bound and increasing accuracy with ensemble size. No experimental result values or entries change.

T1.justification: Section 5.2 corrects addition's maximum unwanted-correlation count from 2 to 1, aligning with the existing appendices. Appendix D.1 replaces the coordinate condition x-hat_i != 0 in the definition of z_i with the matching-indicator condition I_i(x-hat) != 0. The principal theorems and asymptotic bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same exact-learnability and sample-efficiency claims for the four algorithmic tasks. The introduction explicitly mentions iterative composition and polynomial dependence on input bit size, both already documented in v2's framework.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 explicitly distinguishes SBN simulation from directly learning arbitrary computable functions. Section 7 newly explains that increasing memory changes input dimensionality and requires retraining, preventing automatic length extrapolation, and proposes bounded-degree GNNs as a future direction.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly identifies full-batch gradient descent as the optimizer for the existing experiments. Section 6 repeats this information and the previously disclosed 50,000-unit width. The source-code link in Appendix B is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Malach (2023) on autoregressive universal learners and discusses Wei et al. (2022a) as providing statistical learnability guarantees. Wei was previously grouped with Turing-completeness simulations; the revised discussion distinguishes these approaches from exact learnability.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in the introduction, Sections 5.1–5.2, and the limitations section clarify iterative execution, matching weights, and applicability. The overall narrative sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All seven figures and their captions are preserved. Some proof equations are moved inline, and text and mathematical displays reflow around the existing figures; no figure or table is added, removed, or redesigned.

improvement.justification: V3 improves precision through explicit memory and generalization limitations, clearer positioning of SBN simulation, and limited mathematical corrections. Disclosing the optimizer also modestly improves reproducibility. These are useful refinements while the central results and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
